page: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v7 is a compute-focused instance within the general-purpose virtual machine lineup, configured with a lower memory-to-vCPU allocation and integrated local temporary solid-state storage. The virtual machine provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 dedicated physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, running on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include an extensive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is fixed at 32.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per virtual core. High-speed local scratch space is provided by a bundled 944 GB NVMe SSD. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded data manipulation throughput, placing in the top quartile with 32.42 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 13.98 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Small-model edge inference performance is also notable, generating 267.04 tokens per second on a 135M parameter language model. Broader compute and memory metrics register within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud instances, achieving 15,943.77 in multi-core stress-ng, a PassMark CPU score of 26,945.67, and an uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 124.77 GB/sec. Web serving throughput reached 30.27 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations scaled to 27.33 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the reduced 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio makes the instance cost-efficient for workloads prioritizing raw clock speeds and integer processing over expansive in-memory working sets. The primary technical tradeoff is memory capacity; applications with large in-memory footprints risk swapping or out-of-memory states. The local 944 GB NVMe SSD provides fast read and write access for caching or scratch disks, although long-term persistence requires external volumes. Suitable workloads include build automation, batch compression, web application tiers with external caches, CI/CD pipelines, and localized file processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D16lds_v7 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine featuring 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated physical cores on a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the server includes 480 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 extensions. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Fast local storage is bundled via a 944 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated GPUs are absent. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-threaded compression and small-scale language model token generation, alongside standard mid-tier multi-core compute and memory bandwidth results. The hardware profile suits compute-heavy, memory-lean applications such as CI/CD runners, batch processing, compression pipelines, and containerized web application servers that benefit from high CPU clock speeds and low-latency local storage without requiring high RAM density.
